definitions.explanation: The open-hand shape in the game janken, which beats rock (グー) and loses to scissors (チョキ). Also used for an open, spread hand generally.

examples.japanese: パーを{出|だ}して{勝|か}った。
{手|て}をグーからパーに{開|ひら}いて、{子供|こども}に{数|かず}を{教|おし}えた。
examples.english: I opened my hand from a fist to an open palm and taught the child to count.

notes:
One of the three hand shapes in {じゃんけん|じゃんけん} (rock-paper-scissors), together with グー (rock) and チョキ (scissors). パー is a flat open hand; it beats グー and loses to チョキ.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- パーを{出|だ}す: to throw paper
- {手|て}をパーにする: to open the hand flat

USAGE:
In casual speech パーになる separately means "to come to nothing" (e.g. plans falling through), a different, idiomatic sense.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- グー: rock — the clenched-fist shape
- チョキ: scissors — the two-finger shape
